Cheat sheet for contributors reviewing a staged SUMO article in Google Docs. Every token below is shown '''already formatted''' — copy one straight out of this Doc into an article Doc and it keeps its highlight.

==The one rule that matters==
A '''highlighted''' run is wiki source and is copied back out verbatim. Everything else is treated as prose.
*'''Any''' highlight colour counts — the check is only "does this run have a background colour".
*'''Please use the house pale yellow, #FFF2CC''' — the colour the tool applies when it stages a Doc. Others work, but one consistent colour is what makes "don't touch this" readable at a glance.
*Courier New is only a visual cue. The font is not part of the check.

==What survives an edit==
#Highlighted, any colour → comes back '''verbatim''', as wiki source.
#Courier New with '''no''' highlight → comes back as an inline <code>code</code> span.
#Neither → ordinary prose; any wiki meaning is lost.

So edit the words '''around''' a token, never the characters inside it. Highlight a sentence by accident and it will be published as raw markup; delete a token's highlight and the article silently loses that construct. Adding a token by hand is fine: type the wiki text, then highlight it in #FFF2CC.

Two more habits: leave a line that is '''nothing but tokens''' on its own line — that is how the article's structure survives the trip back — and don't tidy a token's spacing or capitalisation, because it is source code, not prose.

==The 16 protected kinds==
These are the labels the tool reports after a conversion ("Protected tokens preserved verbatim").

===Inline===
#{for win,mac} … {/for} — the OS / version conditionals
#{note} … {/note}
#{warning} … {/warning}
#{key Ctrl+T} — a keyboard shortcut
#{menu Account Settings} — a menu path or label
#{button Add WebDAV} — a button label
#{filepath prefs.js} — a file name or path
#{pref mail.server.default} — a preference name or value
#[[Image:Name of screenshot]] — an image from the SUMO gallery
#[[Template:Sample]] and [[Include:Sample]] — templates
#[[How to Use Attachments]] — any other link to a KB article
#__TOC__, __NOTOC__ and friends — the magic words

===Whole blocks, protected in one piece with their line breaks===
13. A wiki table:
{|
! Provider !! Supported
|-
| WebDAV || yes
|}
14. A code block spanning more than one line, which is preformatted on SUMO, so its line breaks and indentation are kept exactly:
<code>
{
  "manifest_version": 2
}
</code>
A '''single-line''' <code>like this</code> is '''not''' a token — it becomes real monospace formatting instead.

15. An HTML comment, including a multi-line one:
<!-- TODO: add a screenshot of the Attachments pane -->
A comment starting <!-- TODO (sumo-kb-tools): --> is a note the tool left for you. Act on it, then delete the comment before publishing.

16. The leading indent and definition-list markers on a line:

:like this one, where only the colon is the token

==What is not a token==
Rendered as normal Doc formatting and converted back automatically: headings, '''bold''', ''italic'', bulleted and numbered lists, external links, a single-line <code>code</code> span, and the inline HTML tags u, s, del, sub, sup, blockquote and br. Edit these like ordinary text.

One known limitation: a sub-bullet nested under a numbered step cannot be shown as a bullet by the Google Docs API, so it appears as a. / b. and converts back as a number. The tool leaves a TODO comment above any list where that happens.
